brief: A new Commerce Department rule closes a loophole that let Chinese firms rent AI compute abroad, and Congress is moving toward a wider four-bill export package the same week Nvidia's chief lobbyist against such curbs departed. Asia's AI-linked markets sold off overnight (Kospi, Taiex, Thailand) while China's domestic chip basket and India, with little AI exposure, both rallied. In the US, equities rotated hard defensive: Goldman's Privorotsky says the utilities-over-bonds premium (XLU over TLT) is near a five-year extreme, yet long-dated Treasuries have not confirmed the growth scare equities are pricing. He argues bonds are waiting on Fed chair Warsh, whose own history and September rate hike show he tracks financial conditions closely, so a break of the Nasdaq 100's recent lows, not a data print, is what would flip the rate-outcome distribution away from hikes. Zero Hedge's own view: equities are right and bonds are late, making the defensive trade a bet that pain comes before any Warsh pivot. Side notes: cyber spending is turning non-discretionary, and Privorotsky flags robotics as an underpriced AI subtheme.
